title: fix: spec requirements collapsed by default — content hidden on open
description:
Every Requirement and Scenario in spec files is wrapped in a <details> element and collapsed by default. Users see only headings like '▶ Issue Loading' with no content visible. A reading app that hides its content is self-defeating.

**File:** src/shared/document-renderer.ts (lines ~42–70, the openspec-details wrapping logic).

**Spec:** Not mandated by openspec/specs/spec-viewer/spec.md — collapsing is an implementation choice, safe to change.

**Fix:** Add the open attribute to the generated <details> element. Change the htmlStart string from '<details class="openspec-details ...' to '<details open class="openspec-details ...'. Users can still collapse individual sections manually. Do NOT add an expand-all button — default-open makes it unnecessary.

**Verification:** Open charly-vibes/atril → Specs → beads-viewer spec. All Requirements and Scenarios must be visible without any clicks. bun test passes.

title: fix: issues view opens with empty right panel — auto-select first issue

**Spec:** openspec/specs/beads-viewer/spec.md §List Detail View — 'the main panel displays the full issue detail' implies an issue must be selected.

**Fix:** After the issue list renders, programmatically select and display the first visible issue (respecting any active filters). On mobile stacked layout, do not auto-scroll to the detail panel — auto-selection only, scroll position stays at top of list.

**Verification:** Navigate to charly-vibes/wai issues view. On load, the first issue in the list is highlighted and its detail appears in the right panel without any user click. bun test passes.

title: fix: loading text renders top-left instead of centered

**Fix:** Center #loading-screen content both horizontally and vertically using flexbox (display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:100vh). Add a subtle CSS pulse/fade animation to the message text to indicate activity.

**Verification:** Load a large repo (e.g. microsoft/vscode) and confirm 'Loading repository…' appears centered on screen during the API fetch. bun test passes.

title: Fix in-app back navigation to be predictable across all views
description:
## Why this exists

Users who drill into a spec or issue cannot reliably get back. The current navDepth counter resets on page load and doesn't track which view they came from — pressing the in-app back button sometimes jumps to overview instead of the previous file.

## What needs to be done

Replace the navDepth integer with a proper navigation stack stored in history.state. Each navigate() call pushes an entry with the full context (view, file, query) onto the stack. The in-app ← button pops one entry and restores the previous view. Browser back and in-app back should behave identically.

## Acceptance criteria

- Navigating from overview → specs-tree → file → cross-link file and pressing ← four times returns to overview step by step
- Reloading the page and pressing ← does not crash or navigate to a wrong place
- Each view's back button correctly identifies where 'back' leads before the user clicks it
notes: State shape for consumers: history.state = { view, fileId, query, scrollY }. atril-xgv (persistent nav) and atril-r2n (breadcrumb) consume this — they must not define their own navigation state format.
close_reason: Implemented and validated via Playwright. navDepth replaced with history.state NavState; contextual back labels; shared-link safety guard; reload-then-back preserved.

title: fix: branch toggle looks like a label — add visible interactive affordance
description:
On the overview screen the current branch name ('main') is displayed in small muted monospace text with no border, chevron, or other affordance indicating it is clickable. It only gains a visible border on hover — completely undiscoverable.

**Files:** src/shared/repo-overview.ts (branch toggle rendering), src/styles.css (.branch-toggle class or equivalent).

**Fix:** At rest (not hovered), the branch toggle must show:
1. A visible downward chevron (▾) after the branch name
2. A subtle border: border: 1px solid var(--color-border); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 6px

Example rendered output: main ▾

This makes the interactive affordance visible without requiring hover.

**Verification:** Load overview for any repo. Branch name shows a chevron and border without hovering. Click it to confirm branch input appears. bun test passes.

title: fix: filter zero-results shows double empty state with no clear-all action
description:
When active filters (status + type + priority) return no issues, the UI shows both 'No issues match the current filters' (left panel) and 'Select an issue to view details' (right panel) simultaneously — a confusing double empty state. There is also no way to clear filters.

**File:** src/shared/beads-renderer.ts (empty-state rendering in beads list/detail view).

**Spec:** openspec/specs/beads-viewer/spec.md §Issue Filtering.

**Depends on:** atril-7lh (search × button, touches same file — land that first).

**Fix:**
1. When the filtered list is empty, render a single centered message across both columns that names the active filters: e.g. 'No issues matching status: open, type: task'.
2. Add a 'Clear filters' link inline with the message that resets all three dropdowns to their default 'All …' state.
3. Hide the right detail panel entirely when the list is empty.

**Verification:** Apply status=open, type=task, priority=P2 on charly-vibes/wai repo. Confirm single centered message naming the active filters. Confirm 'Clear filters' resets all dropdowns. bun test passes.

title: fix: issues search empty state ignores the search term
description:
When a search query returns no results, the message says 'No issues match the current filters' — it does not reference the actual search term. The search box has no × / clear button.

**File:** src/shared/beads-renderer.ts (search input and empty-state message rendering).

**Fix:**
1. When search is non-empty and produces zero results, message should read: No issues matching "<term>" (include the actual search input value).
2. Add a × (clear) button inside the search input (absolute-positioned right side) that appears only when the input has a value. Clicking it clears the search and restores the full list.

**Verification:** Type 'xyznonexistent' in issues search. Confirm message shows 'No issues matching "xyznonexistent"'. Confirm × button appears and clicking it clears the input and restores the list. bun test passes.

title: fix: no share/copy-link affordance for files and issues
description:
Shareable URLs are a core feature of atril — the URL updates with repo, branch, file path, and issue ID — but there is no in-UI affordance to copy or share the current link. Users must know to copy the address bar, which is a power-user behaviour.

**Files:** src/shared/navigation-renderers.ts (file nav bar), src/shared/beads-renderer.ts (issue detail panel).

**Spec:** openspec/specs/beads-viewer/spec.md §Shareable URLs — the system SHALL support shareable URLs.

**Fix:** Add a copy-link button (chain/link icon) to:
1. The file view nav bar — right side alongside the History button
2. The issue detail panel header

On click: navigator.clipboard.writeText(window.location.href). Show a brief 'Copied!' text confirmation (replace button label for 1.5s, then revert). No toast library needed — a CSS class toggle suffices.

**Verification:** Open a spec file, click copy-link, paste URL in new tab → same file loads. Open an issue, click copy-link, paste URL in new tab → same issue selected. bun test passes.

title: F1: Make all interactive elements keyboard-accessible

Interactive items (suggestion list items, tree items, breadcrumb segments) are div/li/span elements with click handlers but no tabindex, no role=button/link, and no keydown handlers for Enter/Space. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users cannot activate any content navigation.

title: docs: apply README front-door standard v0.4 (§5.1)

Audit (2026-11-15): 4/10. Good framing and docs layers, but no way to open/run a viewer.

Repo-specific gaps:
- No URL or run instruction for the spec/beads viewers, and no repo/query parameter example.
- No when-to-use vs the `jams` prototypes or reading specs on GitHub directly.
- No FAQ for GitHub API rate limits, private repos, or branch switching.

Required changes:

- [ ] Make `## Quick start` install → first meaningful command → expected output.
- [ ] Add `## FAQ` (5–7 questions) or link `docs/src/faq.md` / `docs/src/troubleshooting.md` from the README first screen.
- [ ] Move repository-development recipes (`just …`, build-from-source) to `## Development`.
- [ ] Fix broken relative README links (if any).

Release note: §1 now requires prebuilt binaries on GitHub Releases for binary tools (five targets + checksums.txt); non-binary repos record the deviation in `docs/src/status.md`.

Context: fleet README audit 2026-11-15 (45 repos); umbrella epic `charly-o1j`.

title: Add slide-in file tree panel from within spec/doc view
description:
## Why this exists

The user's primary complaint was 'finding documents, exploring the specs.' The current flow requires leaving the spec you're reading to browse the file tree — there's no way to see what's available while staying in context.

## What needs to be done

Add a slide-in (or collapsible sidebar) file tree panel accessible from within any spec or doc view. The panel shows the same directory structure as the full tree view, lets the user open a different file, and can be dismissed to return to reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A toggle button (e.g. folder icon) is visible while reading a spec or doc file
- Clicking it opens a slide-in or sidebar panel showing the file tree for the current category (Specs or Docs)
- Selecting a file from the panel navigates to it (replacing current view)
- Dismissing the panel without selecting returns the user to the same scroll position
- Works on both desktop and mobile viewport widths

title: Add persistent category nav to switch views without returning to overview
description:
## Why this exists

Currently there is no persistent navigation element. To switch from reading a spec to looking at issues, the user must press back repeatedly until they reach overview, then click into issues. This breaks the reading flow and makes the tool feel like a series of dead ends rather than a coherent explorer.

## What needs to be done

Add a persistent navigation bar (top bar or collapsible sidebar) that shows the four main categories: Specs, Docs, Issues, History. The active category is highlighted. Clicking another category switches the main content area while preserving the user's place in the previous category (stored in state so returning to Specs restores where they were).

The nav should also include a Home link that returns to the repo overview.

## Acceptance criteria

- Nav is visible on every screen except the initial repo-entry form
- Clicking a category navigates to that view without passing through overview
- The active category is visually highlighted
- On narrow viewports (<600px) the nav collapses to icons or a hamburger menu
- Navigating away and back to a category restores the last position within that category (best-effort)

title: Redesign overview screen as explorable category cards
description:
## Why this exists

After entering a repo URL the user sees badges and a suggestion list. This is not enough to communicate what's inside the repo or invite exploration. Users want to understand what categories of content exist (Specs, Docs, Issues, History) and how much is there before committing to a click.

## What needs to be done

Replace the badge row on the overview with category cards. Each card shows:
- Category name (Specs, Docs, Issues, History)
- A short count or summary (e.g. '12 spec files', '5 open issues', 'last changed 2d ago')
- A visual indicator if the category has no content (grayed out)
- Clicking the card navigates directly into that category's list/tree

Keep the search input and suggestion list below the cards for quick access.

## Acceptance criteria

- All four categories (Specs, Docs, Issues, History) are shown as cards on the overview
- Each card displays a meaningful count or summary pulled from cached repo data
- Empty categories are visually distinct (grayed, 'not found' label) but still present
- Clicking a card navigates to the matching view (specs tree, docs tree, beads list, history list)
- The layout works at 320px width (single column) and 800px+ (two or four columns)

title: Add cross-screen breadcrumb trail for file and spec navigation
description:
## Why this exists

When a user opens a spec, jumps to a related file, then another cross-link, they lose track of where they started. Each screen shows an isolated breadcrumb (directory segments of the current file) but there is no trail showing the navigation path across files. The user cannot step back through the chain of files they visited.

## What needs to be done

Display a breadcrumb trail above the file/spec content area that reflects the full navigation chain, not just the current file's directory path. Each crumb is clickable and navigates back to that point in the stack. The trail is cleared when the user returns to overview.

Example: Overview > Specs > openspec/ > my-feature.md > related-spec.md

## Acceptance criteria

- After opening a file from the tree and clicking a cross-link, the breadcrumb shows both file names
- Clicking any intermediate crumb restores that file at its previous scroll position (best-effort)
- Navigating back to overview clears the breadcrumb trail
- Trail does not overflow on mobile — truncates with ellipsis on the left

Change proposal: openspec/changes/add-ubiquitous-language-explorer/

title: fix: spec file view has no table of contents for long documents
description:
Long spec files have no table of contents. Users must scroll the entire document to find a section. This is a spec compliance issue — the spec-viewer spec mandates TOC generation.

**Spec:** openspec/specs/spec-viewer/spec.md §Table of Contents — 'The system SHALL auto-generate a table of contents for documents with 3 or more headings.'

**File:** src/shared/document-renderer.ts (markdown rendering pipeline).

**Fix:**
1. After markdown renders, scan the output DOM for all heading elements (h1–h6) that have id attributes.
2. If 3 or more headings exist, generate a <nav class='doc-toc'> with anchor links to each heading, reflecting hierarchy (h2 flush-left, h3 indented, etc.).
3. Insert the TOC before the first heading in the rendered content.
4. If fewer than 3 headings exist, render no TOC.

Note: sticky/collapsible TOC behaviour is NOT in scope for this ticket — that is a separate enhancement if desired.

**Verification:** Open a spec with 3+ headings (e.g. beads-viewer spec). TOC appears at top of content linking to each section. Clicking a TOC link scrolls to that heading. Open a file with <3 headings — no TOC appears. bun test passes.

title: fix: error screen provides no actionable recovery beyond 'Back'
description:
The error screen shows a message (e.g. 'Repository not found.') and a single 'Back' button. No hint about what went wrong, no suggestion to correct it, no pre-filled retry path.

**File:** src/main.ts (error screen rendering, showError or equivalent function).

**Fix:**
1. For 'repository not found' errors: add a hint beneath the error message — 'Check the owner/repo spelling and try again.'
2. Change 'Back' to 'Try again' — returns to the entry screen with the previously attempted repo value pre-filled in the input.
3. For other errors (rate limit, network): add a generic hint — 'This may be a temporary GitHub API issue. Wait a moment and try again.'
4. Store the last attempted repo slug in a variable accessible to the error screen renderer.

**Verification:** Enter a nonexistent repo. Error screen shows 'Repository not found.' with the hint and a 'Try again' button. Clicking 'Try again' returns to entry with the typed repo pre-filled. bun test passes.

title: fix: theme toggle has no icon — text-only and low-opacity is not discoverable
description:
The theme toggle button shows only 'Auto'/'Light'/'Dark' text at ~50% opacity in the top-right corner. No sun/moon icon. Nearly invisible at rest.

**Files:** src/main.ts or src/shared/navigation-renderers.ts (theme toggle button), src/styles.css (theme toggle opacity and style).

**Fix:**
1. Prefix the button label with a mode icon: ☀ for Light, ☾ for Dark, ◑ for Auto (or equivalent SVG icons)
2. Increase default opacity from ~0.5 to 0.8. Keep 1.0 on hover
3. Keep the text label alongside the icon for clarity

**Verification:** Theme button is clearly visible without hovering. Shows appropriate icon for each mode. Cycling Auto→Dark→Light→Auto works correctly. Theme preference persists on reload. bun test passes.

title: fix: freshness indicator shows date without year (e.g. 'Apr 28')
description:
The issues freshness indicator shows 'Loaded from main · Apr 28' with no year. This is ambiguous if viewed in a future session or months later.

**File:** src/shared/beads-renderer.ts (freshness/date formatting logic).

**Fix:** Include the year in the displayed date. Use: date.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }) which produces 'Apr 28, 2026'.

**Verification:** Load issues for any repo. Freshness indicator shows year: 'Loaded from main · Apr 28, 2026'. bun test passes.

title: fix: mobile issues view filter bar wraps to 2 rows, crowding list
description:
On 375px viewport the issues toolbar wraps to two rows: search + status filter on row 1, type + priority filters on row 2. Filter controls dominate before any issue is visible.

**File:** src/styles.css (beads toolbar responsive rules, media query for narrow viewports).

**Fix:** On viewports 480px and below, collapse the three filter dropdowns behind a single 'Filter ▾' toggle button. The search input remains always visible on the toolbar row. The filter button shows a filled dot badge (●) when any filter is non-default (e.g. 'Filter ● ▾'). Tapping Filter opens the dropdowns in a stacked panel below the toolbar.

**Verification:** At 375px viewport, issues toolbar is a single row (search input + Filter button). Tapping Filter reveals the three dropdowns. When a non-default filter is active, the Filter button shows a dot badge. bun test passes.

title: fix: history view shows commit metadata inconsistently
description:
Most commits in the history list show only SHA + title with no author or date visible without expanding. A few show author+date inline. The inconsistency creates an uneven scanning pattern.

**File:** src/shared/history-overview.ts (commit list/summary rendering).

**Fix:** Show author + date for ALL commits inline in the summary row — not just some. Format: {SHA} {title} · {author} · {short-date} on every summary line. If the title is long, truncate it at 60 characters with ellipsis rather than dropping the metadata.

**Verification:** Load charly-vibes/atril → Recent history. Every commit summary line shows SHA, title, author, and date without any expanding. bun test passes.

title: fix: inactive source badges have no affordance or tooltip explaining absence
description:
On repos without specs/issues/memory/docs, those badges are dimmed but still appear to be interactive buttons. Clicking them silently does nothing — no cursor change, no tooltip, no explanation.

**Files:** src/shared/repo-overview.ts (source badge rendering), src/styles.css (inactive badge styles).

**Fix:** Use option (b) — tooltip on hover. Inactive badges should:
1. Render as <span> (not <button>) so they are not in the tab order and cannot be focused
2. Have cursor: default style
3. Have a title attribute: 'No [specs/issues/memory/docs] found in this repository'
4. Keep the existing dimmed visual style

**Verification:** Load torvalds/linux overview. SPECS, ISSUES, MEMORY, DOCS badges are not focusable via Tab. Hovering shows a native tooltip. Clicking does nothing. README badge remains clickable. bun test passes.

title: fix: file search surfaces .wai/ internal notes before source files
description:
Fuzzy file search (e.g. 'router') returns .wai/projects/*/research/ files with long date-prefixed names before actual source files like src/router.ts. Internal wai notes dominate results with low-signal filenames.

**File:** src/shared/file-tree.ts (fuzzyFilterEntries function).

**Fix:** Apply a path-based ranking multiplier: if a file's path starts with a dot-directory (.wai/, .beads/, .github/), multiply its fuzzy score by 0.5, ranking it below source/spec/doc files. Do NOT exclude dot-directory files entirely — they may be legitimately searched. Source files (src/), spec files (openspec/), and docs (docs/) should rank highest.

**Verification:** Search 'router' on charly-vibes/atril. src/shared/router.ts appears in the top 3 results, above any .wai/ files. bun test passes.

title: fix: spec tree shows redundant path context on every item
description:
The canonical specs tree (openspec/specs/) lists items like 'beads-viewer / openspec/specs', 'platform / openspec/specs'. Since all items share the same parent directory, the repeated path below each entry adds zero information — pure visual clutter.

**File:** src/shared/openspec-index.ts or the spec-tree rendering logic in src/main.ts.

**Fix:** When rendering a tree section where all items share the same parent directory, omit the path from individual items and show it once as a section header. Example:

  openspec/specs/
    beads-viewer
    design-system
    platform
    spec-viewer

**Verification:** Load charly-vibes/atril → Specs. The path 'openspec/specs' appears once as a header, not repeated under each item. bun test passes.

title: Add file navigation: browsable file tree and fuzzy search
description:
Currently the overview page only shows a few entry points (README, project.md, issues, wai, docs/). Individual spec files and deeper paths (e.g. openspec/specs/platform/spec.md, openspec/changes/add-unified-repo-reader/specs/repo-overview/spec.md) are only reachable by manually constructing URLs or following inline links. Users need a way to discover and navigate to any file in the repo.

Proposed approach:
- Add a browsable file tree or searchable file index accessible from the overview
- Include fuzzy search (type-ahead) so users can quickly find files by partial name
- The repo tree data is already available (GitHub API getTree), just needs a UI surface

title: Add persistent search bar scoped to current category
description:
## Why this exists

Search is currently a separate view. The agreed spec (ui-align session) called for an always-visible search input, scoped to the current category by default, so users can search without navigating away from what they're doing.

## What needs to be done

Move search input into the persistent nav bar (atril-xgv) or add it as a sticky element within each category view. When the user is in Specs, search returns spec results; in Docs, doc results; etc. A global option can be available as a toggle or fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A search input is visible on every screen without navigating to a dedicated search view
- Submitting a query from inside a category returns results scoped to that category
- Results link directly to the matching file/issue
- The search bar does not obstruct the primary content area on narrow viewports
